It ends in a light front-edge line at row 45, with dark shadow at rows 47-48 above the lower front wall (rows 48-77, about 30 rows). The upper room has a sloped blue tarp roof at rows 0-9, with a light edge line at row 9 and eave shadow at rows 10-12, above its own front wall. styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are close to the references: 13 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, 5% near-flat coverage against 0%, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines are tinted (dark brown beside wood, dark blue beside the tarp) rather than near-black. By eye, the candidate is a small, busy two-level prop-like building. The tarp roof, plywood deck, and planks show about 3-4 lightness steps each, against the 5-6 steps of the reference tile roofs and plaster. Texture is present as plank grain, rust patches and tarp folds, but it is coarser and less varied than the per-tile scallops and per-stone shading of the references. There are no large flat fills, though the plywood deck and parts of the lower wall come close. Overall it is competent and rich enough in tones, but the shading ramps are shallower than Beodeul and the material detail is less refined, so it does not quite match the references.
